stories.title: Is the AI industry really ready to slow down?
stories.simple_summary: AI company leaders are being asked if they really mean it when they say they want to slow down AI development. There's debate about whether they're serious.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and people working in AI companies — it doesn't affect your daily life right now.

stories.title: Vocci’s ring adds a new form factor to meeting note-taking
stories.simple_summary: A company made a ring you wear on your finger that records meeting notes for you. It costs $249.
stories.why_it_matters: If you attend lots of meetings and want an easier way to remember what was said, this might be interesting — but it raises privacy concerns since it's recording conversations.

stories.title: ScrollEd wants to turn textbooks into TikTok
stories.simple_summary: A company is making textbooks look like TikTok and Instagram, with videos and quizzes built in instead of just words on pages.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mainly for students and schools — if you have grandchildren in school, their learning materials might look different in the future.

stories.title: Trump now says he wants to form an ‘AI Force’
stories.simple_summary: The president announced plans to create an "AI Force" and appoint someone to lead AI policy for the government.
stories.why_it_matters: This is political news about government organization — it could eventually affect how AI is regulated, but no immediate changes for you right now.

stories.title: 6 days left to get ahead at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
stories.simple_summary: This is an advertisement for a tech conference with a ticket deadline.
stories.why_it_matters: Unless you're in the tech business, this doesn't matter to you.

stories.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang rejects AI extinction warnings as "doomsday narratives"
stories.simple_summary: A major AI company leader said he disagrees with people who warn that AI could become dangerous.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly insider industry debate — it doesn't affect you today.

stories.title: Trump to host China's Xi Jinping for trade, AI talks
stories.simple_summary: The president plans to meet with China's leader to discuss trade and AI.
stories.why_it_matters: This is political news about international relations — the effects, if any, would take a long time to reach ordinary people.

stories.title: Hackers who broke into OpenAI warn the AI industry has a security problem
stories.simple_summary: Hackers broke into OpenAI (a major AI company) and are warning that AI companies don't have good enough security protection.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows AI companies may be vulnerable to attack — it's a reminder that any company handling important information needs strong security.

stories.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang on artificial intelligence
stories.simple_summary: This appears to be a news interview or segment about AI with a company leader.
stories.why_it_matters: Without more details, it's hard to say what this covers — it depends on what was actually discussed.

stories.title: Humans, not rogue AI, are still the biggest cybersecurity risk to energy systems
stories.simple_summary: Energy companies' power systems are easily hacked by people, not by AI. These systems are in danger and getting worse.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters to everyone — it means the power grid you depend on has security weak spots that criminals could exploit.

stories.title: Jensen Huang says there is '0% chance' AI destroys the world by 2030 — 'We should go as fast as we can, irrespective of anyone else,' dismisses Anthropic doom warnings and rejects new regulations
stories.simple_summary: An AI company leader says he's confident AI won't destroy the world by 2030 and says AI development should move as fast as possible without worrying about safety rules.
stories.why_it_matters: This is insider debate among tech leaders about whether AI needs safety limits — it doesn't directly affect you yet, but it's about policy decisions that could matter later.

stories.title: China’s A.I. Makes a Great Leap Forward. But Its Economy Is Falling Behind.
stories.simple_summary: China has made good progress on AI technology, but its overall economy is still struggling.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly relevant to investors and people who follow international economics — it doesn't directly affect you unless you do business with China.
